project.title: Personal task management system
project.scope: A personal task management system that lets a user manage a personal task list (create, view, update, delete, complete and reopen tasks) and view an aggregated task report. The report supports filtering, searching, sorting, metric counts and Excel export. The backend stores tasks in a new table in the existing database and exposes API endpoints for task management and reporting.
business_goals: Let users track their daily tasks
Let users generate status reports from their tasks

stories.title: Create a task and view the task list
stories.i_want: to create a new task and view the list of tasks
stories.so_that: I can record the work I need to do and see all tasks in one place
stories.business_description: Users can add a task with a title, description, status, priority, creation date and due date, and can view all saved tasks in a list. Each task has a unique ID. A task cannot be saved without a title, and its due date cannot be earlier than its creation date. The frontend shows a success or error message after each create action and never shows a success state before the backend confirms the save.
stories.business_value: Users can capture tasks and see them in one list, which is the base for the update, delete, status and reporting features.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user on the create task form with a non-empty title, a Status of Open, a Priority of Medium and a Due Date equal to or later than today
acceptance_criteria.when: the user submits the form and the backend confirms the save
acceptance_criteria.then: the task is saved with a unique ID, a Creation Date set by the backend, and a success message is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a user on the create task form with an empty title
acceptance_criteria.when: the user submits the form
acceptance_criteria.then: the task is not saved, no success message is shown, and an error message stating that the title is mandatory is displayed

acceptance_criteria.given: a user submits a task whose Due Date is earlier than its Creation Date
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend receives the request
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend rejects it with a simple validation error, the task is not saved, and the frontend shows an error message

acceptance_criteria.given: the backend fails to save a task because of a database error
acceptance_criteria.when: the user submits the create task form
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend shows an error message and does not show a success message or add the task to the list

acceptance_criteria.given: at least one task is saved
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens the task list
acceptance_criteria.then: every saved task is shown with its ID, Title, Description, Status, Priority, Creation Date and Due Date

acceptance_criteria.given: no tasks are saved
acceptance_criteria.when: the user opens the task list
acceptance_criteria.then: the list is empty and the response contains an empty collection rather than an error

acceptance_criteria.given: a create request is submitted with a Status or Priority value outside Open, In Progress, Completed or Low, Medium, High
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend receives the request
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend rejects the request with a simple invalid input error and does not save the task

edge_cases: Title containing only whitespace: the PRD requires a non-empty title; it does not state whether whitespace-only titles are allowed. Open question: treat whitespace-only as empty?
Due Date equal to the Creation Date must be accepted, because the rule only forbids dates earlier than the Creation Date.
Open question: the PRD does not say whether Due Date is mandatory. It is listed as a field but not in the validation rules.
Open question: the PRD does not state whether Description is mandatory, optional, or has a maximum length.
Open question: the PRD does not state the default Status and Priority for a new task. This story assumes the form must send a value.
Open question: the PRD does not define the order of the task list or whether it is paginated.
Open question: the PRD requires endpoints for read by ID, update, delete and status change, but this story only covers create and read all. Confirm which story delivers the other endpoints.
Open question: the PRD does not define the time zone used to compare Due Date with Creation Date.
definition_of_done: Migration creates a new tasks table with columns for unique ID, Title, Description, Status (Open, In Progress, Completed), Priority (Low, Medium, High), Creation Date and Due Date, and runs on the existing database.
POST endpoint creates a task and returns the saved task with its ID and Creation Date.
POST endpoint rejects empty titles and Due Dates earlier than Creation Date, with simple error responses.
GET endpoint returns all saved tasks.
Error responses cover invalid input, missing mandatory fields and internal or database errors.
Create task form shows a success message after the backend confirms the save and an error message after a failure.
Task list displays all required fields for each task.
Automated tests pass for create, list, validation and error cases.
Open questions listed in edge cases are answered or recorded in the story before release.

stories.title: Update the details of an existing task
stories.i_want: to update the details of an existing task
stories.so_that: my task information stays accurate and current
stories.business_description: Users can change the details of a task after it has been created. Each task keeps a Last Updated Date that reflects the most recent update. Updates must keep the task title non-empty and the Due Date not earlier than the Creation Date. The frontend shows a success or error message after each update and shows success only after the backend confirms the change.
stories.business_value: Users keep task records accurate over time, so the task list and task report reflect current work.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task with a non-empty title
acceptance_criteria.when: the user changes the title to another non-empty value and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend confirms the update, the task shows the new title, and the Last Updated Date is set to the time of the save

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task
acceptance_criteria.when: the user clears the title field and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: the task is not saved, the backend returns a validation error for the missing title, and the frontend shows an error message and keeps the previous title

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task with Creation Date 2024-03-01 and Due Date 2024-03-10
acceptance_criteria.when: the user sets the Due Date to 2024-02-28 and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: the update is rejected with a validation error, the frontend shows an error message, and the stored Due Date remains 2024-03-10

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task
acceptance_criteria.when: the user saves a valid update and the backend confirms it
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend shows a success message and the Last Updated Date is changed

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing task
acceptance_criteria.when: the user saves an update and the backend returns an error or cannot be reached
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend shows an error message, does not show a success message, and does not display the unsaved changes as saved

acceptance_criteria.given: a task ID that does not exist
acceptance_criteria.when: a client sends an update request for that ID
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend returns a simple not-found error and stores nothing

edge_cases: Title containing only whitespace: the PRD says the title must be non-empty but does not state whether whitespace-only titles are allowed; this is an open question.
Due Date equal to Creation Date: the PRD says Due Date must not be earlier than Creation Date, so equal dates are allowed.
Updating a task that was deleted by another user: the backend returns a not-found error for the update.
Update request with a Due Date but no change to other fields: the PRD does not state whether Last Updated Date changes when nothing changed; this is an open question.
Whether the Creation Date itself can be updated is not stated in the PRD; this is an open question.
Concurrent updates to the same task: the PRD does not define conflict handling; this is an open question.
The exact field list that is editable on update is not enumerated in the PRD beyond title and Due Date; this is an open question.
definition_of_done: Backend update endpoint for a task by ID is implemented and returns the updated task on success
Backend rejects an empty or missing title with a simple validation error
Backend rejects a Due Date earlier than the Creation Date with a simple validation error
Backend returns a simple not-found error for a non-existent task ID
Last Updated Date is set by the backend on each successful update
Frontend shows a success message only after the backend confirms the update
Frontend shows an error message on any backend failure and does not show a successful state
Automated tests cover valid update, empty title, Due Date before Creation Date, and not-found cases
Open questions about whitespace-only titles, no-change updates, and editable fields are documented and resolved with the product owner

stories.title: Delete a task after confirming the deletion
stories.i_want: to delete a task after confirming the deletion in a prompt
stories.so_that: tasks I no longer need are removed from my task list and I am not deleted by accident
stories.business_description: Users can delete a task. Before the deletion is applied, a confirmation prompt must be accepted. The frontend shows a success or error message after the delete action, and it shows success only after the backend confirms the deletion. The backend exposes a delete endpoint and returns simple error responses for a missing task and for internal or database errors.
stories.business_value: Users can remove tasks they no longer need. The confirmation prompt prevents accidental data loss, and the success or error message tells the user the actual outcome.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is shown in the task list
acceptance_criteria.when: the user chooses delete on that task
acceptance_criteria.then: a confirmation prompt is shown and the task is still listed until the user confirms

acceptance_criteria.given: the confirmation prompt is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user confirms the deletion
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend sends the delete request and the task is removed from the list only after the backend returns success

acceptance_criteria.given: the confirmation prompt is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user cancels the prompt
acceptance_criteria.then: no delete request is sent and the task remains unchanged in the list

acceptance_criteria.given: a task has been deleted successfully by the backend
acceptance_criteria.when: the delete response is received
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend shows a success message stating the task was deleted

acceptance_criteria.given: the user confirmed the deletion and the backend returns an error
acceptance_criteria.when: the error response is received
acceptance_criteria.then: the frontend shows an error message, keeps the task in the list and does not show a success state

acceptance_criteria.given: a delete request is sent for a task ID that does not exist
acceptance_criteria.when: the backend receives the request
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend returns a simple not-found error response and does not change any stored task

acceptance_criteria.given: the backend cannot complete the delete because of an internal or database error
acceptance_criteria.when: the request is processed
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend returns a simple internal error response and the task remains stored unchanged

edge_cases: User cancels the confirmation prompt: no request is sent and no message about a deletion is shown.
User confirms twice quickly: the PRD does not state how a repeated delete is handled; the second request is expected to return the not-found error, which needs to be confirmed.

Delete request for a task that was already deleted by another session: the backend returns the not-found error, and the frontend must show an error message rather than success. How the list refreshes in this case is not stated in the PRD and needs a decision.
Backend error during delete: the task must remain in the list and no success state may be shown.
Open question: the PRD does not state whether a deleted task can be restored or whether deletion is permanent; this story assumes permanent deletion until clarified.
Open question: the PRD does not define the exact wording of the confirmation prompt or the success and error messages.
definition_of_done: DELETE endpoint for a single task is implemented and documented with its success and error responses
Not-found and internal or database error responses return simple error bodies as defined in the PRD
Delete action in the UI opens a confirmation prompt that must be accepted before any request is sent
Frontend removes the task from the list only after a successful backend response
Success or error message is shown after every delete attempt
Frontend never shows a success state when the backend returns an error
Automated tests cover confirm, cancel, success, not-found and internal error paths
Open questions about repeated delete and permanence are recorded and answered by the product owner

stories.title: Mark a task as Completed or revert it to Open
stories.i_want: to mark a task as Completed and revert a Completed task back to Open
stories.so_that: I can record which work is finished and reopen work that needs more effort
stories.business_description: Users change the Status of a task between Open and Completed. Completing a task records a Completion Date. Reverting a Completed task sets its Status back to Open. Every change updates the Last Updated Date. The frontend shows a success or error message after each change and never shows a success state before the backend confirms it.
stories.business_value: Users can see which tasks are finished and reopen tasks that were completed too early, so the task list reflects the actual state of the work.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with Status Open exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the user marks the task as Completed and the backend confirms the change
acceptance_criteria.then: the task Status is Completed, the Completion Date is set to the date of the change, and a success message is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with Status Completed exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the user reverts the task to Open and the backend confirms the change
acceptance_criteria.then: the task Status is Open and a success message is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with Status Open exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the user marks the task as Completed and the backend returns an error
acceptance_criteria.then: the task Status remains Open, the UI does not show the task as Completed, and an error message is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a task with Status Completed exists
acceptance_criteria.when: the user reverts the task and the backend returns an error
acceptance_criteria.then: the task Status remains Completed, the UI does not show the task as Open, and an error message is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: a task is marked as Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: the status change is saved
acceptance_criteria.then: the Last Updated Date of the task is set to the time of the change

acceptance_criteria.given: a task ID that does not exist
acceptance_criteria.when: a status change request is sent for that ID
acceptance_criteria.then: the backend returns a Task Not Found error response

edge_cases: Completing a task that is already Completed: the PRD does not state the expected result. Open question: reject, ignore, or keep the original Completion Date.
Reverting a task that is already Open: the PRD does not state the expected result. Open question.
Completion Date after a revert: the PRD does not say whether it is cleared or kept. Open question.
The PRD lists In Progress as a valid Status but does not say how a task enters or leaves In Progress. This story covers only Completed and Open.
Status change request for a task that was deleted by another user: the backend returns a Task Not Found error and the frontend shows an error message.
Backend unavailable or database error during a status change: the backend returns an internal error and the frontend shows an error message without changing the displayed status.
definition_of_done: Status field with allowed values Open, In Progress and Completed exists on every task
Completion Date and Last Updated Date fields exist on every task
Status change endpoint accepts Completed and Open and returns the updated task
Error responses for Task Not Found and invalid input are returned in the simple format defined in the PRD
Frontend shows a success or error message after each status change
Frontend does not show a success state before the backend confirms the change
Automated tests pass for all acceptance criteria

stories.title: Review the task report with task counts
stories.i_want: to review all tasks in a table on the reporting page, with Total, Open and Completed task counts
stories.so_that: I can see the overall status of the work at a glance
stories.business_description: The task report page lists all tasks in a table and shows counts of Total Tasks, Open Tasks and Completed Tasks. The backend exposes a report API that provides the task data and the metric aggregation used on the page.
stories.business_value: Reviewers can see how many tasks exist and how many are open or completed without counting rows by hand.

acceptance_criteria.given: at least one task exists in the system
acceptance_criteria.when: a user opens the reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: every task is shown as a row in a table, and each row shows the task's fields as defined in the task list

acceptance_criteria.given: 5 tasks exist, 2 with status Open and 3 with status Completed
acceptance_criteria.when: a user opens the reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: the page shows Total Tasks = 5, Open Tasks = 2 and Completed Tasks = 3

acceptance_criteria.given: no tasks exist
acceptance_criteria.when: a user opens the reporting page
acceptance_criteria.then: the table shows no rows and the page shows Total Tasks = 0, Open Tasks = 0 and Completed Tasks = 0

acceptance_criteria.given: the task report API is called
acceptance_criteria.when: the request is answered
acceptance_criteria.then: the response contains the task rows and the Total, Open and Completed counts, and the counts equal the number of returned tasks grouped by status

edge_cases: No tasks exist: the table is empty and all three counts are 0.
Total Tasks must equal Open Tasks plus Completed Tasks, provided every task has exactly one of the two statuses. The PRD does not define other statuses; if others exist, this must be clarified.
Open question: the PRD does not state whether deleted tasks are counted or whether counts respect the filters and search defined in the filter story. This story assumes counts cover all tasks.
Open question: the PRD does not state whether the report API must accept filter, search and sort parameters in this story or only in the filter story.
definition_of_done: The task report table shows every task returned by the report API.
Total Tasks, Open Tasks and Completed Tasks are shown on the reporting page and match the API response.
The report API returns the task rows and the three counts in one response.
Counts are 0 when no tasks exist.
Automated tests cover the table, the counts and the empty state.

stories.title: Filter, search and sort the task report
stories.as_a: a team member reviewing the task report
stories.i_want: to filter, search and sort the tasks in the task report
stories.so_that: I can find specific tasks by status, priority, date range or title
stories.business_description: The task report shows all tasks in a table. Users can narrow the list by Status, Priority and Date Range, search by task title, and sort by Creation Date, Due Date, Status or Priority. The backend provides the APIs that support filtering, searching, sorting and metric aggregation for the report.
stories.business_value: Users can locate the tasks they need in the report without scanning every row.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task report containing tasks with different statuses
acceptance_criteria.when: the user selects one Status value in the Status filter
acceptance_criteria.then: only tasks with that Status are listed in the table

acceptance_criteria.given: a task report containing tasks with different priorities
acceptance_criteria.when: the user selects one Priority value in the Priority filter
acceptance_criteria.then: only tasks with that Priority are listed in the table

acceptance_criteria.given: a task report containing tasks with dates inside and outside a chosen range
acceptance_criteria.when: the user sets a Date Range filter
acceptance_criteria.then: only tasks whose date falls inside the range are listed in the table

acceptance_criteria.given: tasks titled 'Quarterly report' and 'Budget review' in the task report
acceptance_criteria.when: the user enters 'report' in the title search
acceptance_criteria.then: only the task titled 'Quarterly report' is listed in the table

acceptance_criteria.given: a task report with several tasks listed
acceptance_criteria.when: the user sorts by Creation Date, Due Date, Status or Priority
acceptance_criteria.then: the table rows are ordered by the selected field

acceptance_criteria.given: the reporting page is opened and tasks exist
acceptance_criteria.when: the page finishes loading
acceptance_criteria.then: every task is shown as one row in the table

acceptance_criteria.given: the task report API receives a request with filter, search and sort parameters
acceptance_criteria.when: the request is processed
acceptance_criteria.then: the response contains only the tasks that match all supplied parameters, in the requested sort order

edge_cases: The PRD does not state which date Date Range applies to (creation date, due date or both). To be confirmed before build.
The PRD does not state whether several filters combine with AND logic. To be confirmed.
The PRD does not state the title search rules (case sensitivity, partial or whole-word match). To be confirmed.
The PRD does not state the sort direction or the default sort order. To be confirmed.
The PRD does not define the ranking order of Status or Priority values when sorting. To be confirmed.
When no task matches the filters or search, the table has no rows. The PRD does not define an empty-state message.
If a task has no due date, the PRD does not state where it appears when sorting by Due Date.
The PRD does not state what happens when Date Range start is later than its end. To be confirmed.
definition_of_done: Filter by Status, Priority and Date Range returns the expected rows in automated tests
Title search returns the expected rows in automated tests
Sorting by Creation Date, Due Date, Status and Priority is verified in automated tests
Task report API accepts filter, search and sort parameters and is documented
Reporting page table shows all tasks and is verified in a manual or automated check
Open questions from the edge cases list are answered and recorded in the story

stories.title: Export the current task report view to Excel
stories.as_a: project member who reviews task reports
stories.i_want: to download the current task report view as an Excel file
stories.so_that: I can share or analyse the filtered and sorted task data outside the application
stories.business_description: Users can export the task report data to Excel. The exported file contains only the rows that match the currently applied filters, in the currently applied sort order. The file has clear column headers, one consistent date format, and a file name that includes the generation timestamp. If there is no data to export, the user sees a message and no file is produced.
stories.business_value: Users can take task report data out of the application for sharing and offline analysis, and the exported data matches what they see on screen.

acceptance_criteria.given: a task report with at least one row is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: the user selects the Export to Excel action
acceptance_criteria.then: an Excel file is downloaded to the user's device

acceptance_criteria.given: a task report with filters and a sort order applied
acceptance_criteria.when: the user exports the report to Excel
acceptance_criteria.then: the file contains only the rows matching the applied filters, in the same order as the applied sort

acceptance_criteria.given: an exported Excel file with date columns
acceptance_criteria.when: the file is opened
acceptance_criteria.then: the header row has a label for every column and every date column uses the same date format

acceptance_criteria.given: a user exports the report at a known generation time
acceptance_criteria.when: the file is downloaded
acceptance_criteria.then: the file name contains the timestamp of the generation time

acceptance_criteria.given: the current filters return zero rows
acceptance_criteria.when: the user selects the Export to Excel action
acceptance_criteria.then: no file is downloaded and a message informing the user that there is no data to export is shown

acceptance_criteria.given: the team has recorded its decision on where the Excel file is generated
acceptance_criteria.when: the user exports the report
acceptance_criteria.then: the file content and file name are the same whichever side generates the file

edge_cases: Filters return zero rows: no file is produced and a message is shown. The message wording is not specified in the PRD and needs a decision.
The exact date format for date columns is not specified in the PRD and needs a decision.
The exact timestamp format used in the file name is not specified in the PRD and needs a decision.
Export is requested while the filters or sort are changing: the PRD does not define which state is exported.
Very large result sets: the PRD does not define a maximum number of rows or a size limit for export.
definition_of_done: Export action downloads an .xlsx file containing the filtered and sorted rows
Exported file has a header row with clear column labels
All date columns use one documented date format
File name includes the generation timestamp in a documented format
Zero-row export shows a user message and produces no file
Decision on frontend or backend generation is recorded and implemented
Automated tests cover filtering, sorting, headers, date format, file name and empty-data behaviour

tasks.title: [BE] Add tasks table migration with ID, Title, Description, Status, Priority and date fields
tasks.description: Create a new table in the existing database with a unique ID, Title, Description, Status (Open, In Progress, Completed), Priority (Low, Medium, High), Creation Date and Due Date. Add a check constraint for the allowed Status and Priority values.
definition_of_done: Migration runs on the existing database and creates the tasks table.
Unique ID is the primary key.
Status and Priority columns reject values outside the allowed sets.
Migration has a tested rollback.

Due Date earlier than Creation Date is rejected and nothing is saved.

requirements.source_quote: A personal task management system that allows users to track daily tasks and generate status reports.
requirements.statement: Describes the product as a personal task management system for tracking daily tasks and generating status reports.
requirements.context_reason: Introductory product description; it states the product purpose but no testable requirement.

requirements.source_quote: The system consists of two main pages.
requirements.statement: The system is composed of two main pages.
requirements.context_reason: Descriptive statement about system structure; the pages themselves are not specified in this section.

requirements.source_quote: This page allows the user to manage their personal task list.
requirements.statement: Not a requirement; describes the purpose of the To-Do Management page.
requirements.context_reason: Introductory text that states the page's purpose but no testable requirement.

requirements.statement: Users can create a new task.
Users can view the task list.
Users can update an existing task.
Users can delete a task.
Users can mark a task as 'Completed'.
Users can revert a 'Completed' task back to 'Open'.
Lead-in sentence listing the fields each task must contain; the listed items are the requirements.
requirements.context_reason: Lead-in sentence for the list of task fields; the individual fields are captured as separate requirements.

requirements.statement: Each task has a unique ID field.
Each task has a Title field.
Each task has a Description field.
Each task has a Status field whose allowed values are Open, In Progress and Completed.
Each task has a Priority field whose allowed values are Low, Medium and High.
Each task has a Creation Date field.
Each task has a Due Date field.
Each task has a Last Updated Date field.
Each task has a Completion Date field, populated when the task is completed.

requirements.source_quote: Task titles are mandatory; cannot be empty.
requirements.statement: A task must not be saved unless its title is non-empty.

requirements.source_quote: Due Date cannot be earlier than the Creation Date.
requirements.statement: A task's Due Date must not be earlier than its Creation Date.

requirements.source_quote: Deleting a task requires a prompt confirmation.
requirements.statement: Deleting a task requires the user to confirm the deletion through a prompt before it is applied.

requirements.source_quote: Success or error messages must be displayed after create/update/delete actions.
requirements.statement: A success or error message must be displayed after each create, update, or delete task action.

requirements.source_quote: Optimistic UI updates are not allowed: if a Backend action fails, the Frontend must not reflect a successful state.
requirements.statement: The frontend must not show a successful state for a task change before the backend confirms it, and must not show success when a backend action fails.
Task list view.
requirements.context_reason: Heading-like label without a testable requirement.

requirements.source_quote: The Todos should be saved in persistence DB – assume the DB already exits but there will be a need for a new table
requirements.statement: Todos are persisted in the existing database in a new table created for them.

requirements.source_quote: Endpoints for Create, Read (All & By ID), Update, Delete, and Status Change.
requirements.statement: The backend exposes endpoints to create, read all, read by ID, update, delete, and change the status of a Todo.

requirements.source_quote: Error handling for: Task Not Found, Invalid Input, Missing Mandatory Fields, Deleting/Updating Non-Existent Tasks, and Internal Server/Database Errors. For error handling - Keep it simple
requirements.statement: The backend returns simple error responses for task not found, invalid input, missing mandatory fields, updating or deleting non-existent tasks, and internal server or database errors.

requirements.source_quote: This page presents an aggregated view of the user's tasks.
requirements.statement: This page presents an aggregated view of the user's tasks.
requirements.context_reason: Introductory text that describes the page's purpose but states no testable requirement.

requirements.statement: The reporting page displays all tasks in a table.
The task report can be filtered by Status, Priority, and Date Range.
The task report can be searched by task title.

requirements.source_quote: Sort: By Creation Date, Due Date, Status, or Priority.
requirements.statement: The task report can be sorted by Creation Date, Due Date, Status, or Priority.

requirements.source_quote: Metrics: Total Tasks, Open Tasks, Completed Tasks.
requirements.statement: The task report shows the counts of Total Tasks, Open Tasks, and Completed Tasks.
The user can download task report data as an Excel file.

requirements.source_quote: The file must reflect the currently applied filters and sorting.
requirements.statement: The exported Excel file must contain only the rows matching the currently applied filters, in the currently applied sort order.

requirements.source_quote: Clear column headers and consistent date formatting.
requirements.statement: The exported Excel file must have clear column headers and use one consistent date format across all date columns.

requirements.source_quote: Filename must include the generation timestamp.
requirements.statement: The exported Excel file name must include the timestamp of when the file was generated.

requirements.source_quote: User-friendly message if there is no data to export.
requirements.statement: When there is no data to export, the system must show a message to the user instead of producing an export file; the message text is not specified in the PRD.

requirements.source_quote: APIs to support filtering, searching, sorting, and metric aggregation.
requirements.statement: The system exposes APIs that support filtering, searching, sorting, and metric aggregation for task reporting.

requirements.source_quote: The architectural decision of whether to generate the Excel file on the Frontend or Backend is left to the development team.
requirements.statement: The development team decides whether the Excel file is generated on the frontend or the backend.
